subject.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unsupported OAuth enterprise domain before refresh and model routing

question: Should OpenClaw permanently disable login, refresh, and model routing for legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth credentials whose persisted origin is outside github.com and single-label *.ghe.com tenants, while continuing to trust token proxy endpoints only for allowlisted origins?
rationale: The code safely enforces a coherent boundary, but accepting the resulting upgrade break and the remaining proxy-endpoint trust model requires provider/security ownership rather than automation judgment.

options.title: Confirm boundary and land
options.body: Accept the fail-closed behavior and merge after confirming or adding focused proof that re-authentication replaces or safely coexists with the rejected legacy profile.

options.title: Retire the legacy path
options.body: Pause this patch and move invalid legacy-profile detection and cleanup into the GitHub Copilot plugin's doctor/migration contract before deleting the core OAuth route.

options.title: Keep legacy behavior
options.body: Decline the compatibility break, which preserves existing profiles but also preserves the demonstrated bearer-token egress risk.

recommendation.title: Confirm boundary and land
recommendation.body: Accept the fail-closed behavior and merge after confirming or adding focused proof that re-authentication replaces or safely coexists with the rejected legacy profile.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to Copilot provider behavior, documentation, and the adjacent current-main refactors.
